title: Tenant-aware timeslice arbitration and KV-conscious GPU memory reclamation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Replace coarse preemption buckets with a tenant-aware time-slicing arbitration layer that cooperates with KV-cache residency policies to reduce tail latency and avoid KV thrash on multi-tenant GPU nodes. The feature targets production Dedicated and Hosted nodes running the continuous batching runtime. Goals: 1) ensure SLO-bound tenants keep progress without starving best-effort workloads; 2) reduce KV eviction-induced latency spikes by making reclaim decisions KV-hit-rate aware; 3) provide telemetry and knobs for ops to tune trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Implement timeslice arbitration that assigns per-tenant timeslices proportional to SLO slack and recent token throughput.
KV eviction policy augmented to mark low-hit slabs as reclaimable and avoid reclaiming slabs with high long-tail hit rates.
Preemption should be interruptible with safe KV checkpointing so interrupted requests can resume without a full priming pass.
Show production-like canary results with <=5% increase in average latency and >=10% reduction in p99 spikes from KV thrash compared to baseline.
Runtime exposes metrics: tenant_timeslice_ms, tenant_deficit_score, kv_eviction_rate_per_min, kv_hit_rate_by_slab, gpu_mem_churn, preemptions_count, resumed_requests_success_rate.
Design doc and rollout plan reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after postmortem for intermittent p99 spikes on shared gpu-03. Root cause correlated to aggressive KV eviction during heavy multi-tenant bursts.
2026-03-03 - Arjun Patel: Spike analysis: tenants with tight p95 SLOs were getting preempted by large best-effort batches; observed KV eviction frequency doubled during mixed workload window.

2026-03-04 - Design note: propose deficit-round-robin style timeslices where weight = max(1, floor(slo_slack_ratio*10)). SLO slack derived from moving-window SLO_violation_rate and configured target latency.
2026-03-05 - Experiment: mocked timeslice allocator in staging; results show improved tail fairness but increased context switch overhead ~2%. Need to optimize checkpointing path.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423 — initial timeslice allocator + KV slab tagging. Added feature flag runtime.timeslice_tenant_arbitration.

2026-03-08 - Performance note: initial KV reclaim made up of whole-slab evictions caused priming cost; changed to tiered reclaim (evict cold entries first, then slabs) which reduced priming tokens by ~18% in staging.

2026-03-10 - Security/ops: Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/TC-61257-timeslice-kv-reclaim — includes rollout checklist and SLO definitions. Linking canary dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/canaries/tenant-timeslice-kv. Ops requested a hard disable flag for legacy dedicated clusters.

2026-03-10 - Next steps assigned: (1) optimize interruptible checkpoint to reduce resume overhead, (2) add hysteresis to KV slab reclaim to prevent oscillation, (3) run 72h canary on two Dedicated clusters with mixed tenants.
